questions.text:
Directions: Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. If the sentence is error-free, select No error or option 5. Ignore errors of punctuation if any. 

They occupy (A)/ an house next (B)/ door without paying (C)/ any rent. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the noun 'house' is a specified noun.
    • The noun 'house' is a particular or specific house i.e. the house next door.
  • The definite article 'the' is used before singular and plural nouns when the noun is specific or particular.
  • 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, which means that they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
    • We use 'a' before a consonant sound and we use 'an' before a vowel sound.
  • ''No article'' is used when we refer to general ideas, plurals, or uncountable nouns.
  • Therefore, the definite article 'the' should be used in place of the indefinite article 'an'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Sentence: They occupy the house next door without paying any rent.

Additional Information

There are three articles: a, an, and the. Articles are used before nouns or noun equivalents and are a type of adjective.

RULES COUNT NOUNS NON-COUNT NOUNS
Specific identity not known a, an (no article)
Specific identity is known the the
All things or things in general (no article) (no article)

    • For example:

  • So, considering the context of the sentence, the word that aligns best with the potential impact of AI's speed and efficiency on scientific breakthroughs is "expedite." questions.text: Which of the following words is opposite in meaning to "amalgamation" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the highlighted word "amalgamation" in the context of the passage:
  • Amalgamation - the merging or combining of different elements into a unified whole (संकलन)
    • For Example -
    • The festival was an amalgamation of diverse cultural traditions.
  • Now, let's consider the options:
  • Fusion - similar to amalgamation, meaning the merging or blending of elements (मिलाप)
    • For Example -
    • The fusion of different cuisines created a unique dining experience.
  • Harmony - unrelated to the process of combining different elements; refers to agreement or compatibility (सामंजस्य)
    • For Example -
    • The music concert showcased a beautiful harmony among the instruments.
  • Integration - similar to amalgamation, indicating the combining or unification of parts (एकीकरण)
    • For Example -
    • The integration of new technologies streamlined the workflow.
  • Segregation - opposite of amalgamation, meaning the separation or division of elements (विभाजन)
    • For Example -
    • Segregation based on race was a prevalent issue in history.
  • Comprehension - unrelated to the act of merging or combining; refers to understanding or grasping of something (समझ)
    • For Example -
    • The students showed excellent comprehension of the complex topic.
  • So, after understanding the meaning of "amalgamation" and analyzing the options, we can conclude that the word opposite in meaning to "amalgamation" in the context of the passage is "Segregation." Amalgamation signifies the merging or unification of elements, while segregation denotes the separation or division.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Segregation."

questions.text:
Directions: The following question has two blanks, each blank indicating that something has been omitted. Choose the set of words for each blank that best fits in the context of the sentence.

When University Grants Commission (UGC) _________  that all universities and higher education colleges in India have to _______ security and issue QR code-based degree certificates, it is only a formalization of something that has been long pending.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. 'mandates and incorporate'

Key Points

  • In the first blank we need a singular verb because there is a singular subject i.e. 'University Grants Commission'.
  • In the second blank, we need a verb because of the preposition 'to' it will make an infinitive.
  • Let's see the meanings of the given words:
    • Mandate: is a verb which means 'give authority to act in a certain way.'
    • Incorporate: is a verb which means 'Constitute as a legal corporation.'
    • Deviates: is a verb which means 'diverge from an established course or from usual or accepted standards.'
    • Cooperate: is a verb which means 'work together or help someone.'
    • Delegate: is a verb which means 'entrust a task or something to a person.'
    • Separate: is a verb which means 'move or come apart.'
    • Accentuate: is a verb which means 'make more noticeable or prominent.'
    • Develop: is a verb which means 'grow or cause to grow.'

Important Points

  • As it was written in the explanation, we need a singular verb and all the options have verbs. 
  • But Option 1 and 4 are eliminated because we need a present indefinite tense. 
  • Option 1 is not possible as it is a past tense verb, on the other hand, Option 4 has a plural verb.
  • Option 2, 3, and 5 have singular verbs now we'll check the meanings of the words and we find that the most appropriate according to the meaning is option 2.

The correct sentence is: When University Grants Commission (UGC) mandates that all universities and higher education colleges in India have to incorporate security and issue QR code-based degree certificates, it is only a formalization of something that has been long pending.

    • The second option is incorrect as 'exported' is used as a past form of the verb and 'challenges' is used as a plural form of the noun 'challenge' means a task or situation that tests someone's abilities.
    • The third option is correct as 'export' is used as an adjective describing the noun 'market'. 'Challenging' is used as an adjective modified by the adverb 'very'.

Aegis

B: Due to heavy rain, the event took place under the aegis to ensure the comfort of the guests.

options.text: Both A & C
Only C
All A, B & C

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word given in the question:
  • Aegis: protection, backing, or support of a particular person or organization. (संरक्षण, समर्थन)
  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:
  • Sentence A: The new environmental policy was developed under the aegis of the United Nations.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "aegis" to describe the development of a policy under the support or protection of the United Nations.
  • Sentence B: Due to heavy rain, the event took place under the aegis to ensure the comfort of the guests.
    • This sentence incorrectly uses the word "aegis" as it does not convey the idea of protection or support by an organization or person.
  • Sentence C: The team worked tirelessly under the aegis of the manager to complete the project on time.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "aegis" to describe the team's work under the support and guidance of the manager.
  • So, both sentences A and C correctly use the word "aegis" to illustrate contexts of support or protection.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & C."

  • The sentence 'b' talks about a car accident, in which Steve obtained a head injury that affected his awareness and prevented him from learning new things.

    • Information - Knowledge or facts. (जानकारी या तथ्‍य)
    • Acquired - To obtain something. (कुछ अर्जित करना या ख़रीदना)

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

I. C and A are immediate neighbours. D does not sit adjacent to B.

II. A sits opposite H. D is not a neighbour of E.

options.text: Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

Eight persons:  A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H

ii) G sits third to the right of E.

iii) Two persons sit between E and F.

C and A are immediate neighbours. D does not sit adjacent to B.

Here, the position of A with respect to F cannot be determined.

Therefore, the statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

Considering statement II alone:

II. A sits opposite H. D is not a neighbour of E.

Hence, the statement I and II together are necessary to answer the question.

questions.text: If the total number of printers sold in April is 124 more than the average number of printers sold by the shopkeepers from January to March then What is the total number of printers sold in April month?
questions.explanation:
Let the number of 'Inkjet' printers sold in January = 5x

The number of 'Laser' printers sold in January = 5x - 120

The total number of printers sold in January = 5x + 5x - 120 = 10x - 120

The number of 'Inkjet' printers sold in February = 60% × 5x = 3x

The total number of printers sold in February is 1224 and the total number of printers sold in February is 32% less than that in January.

Therefore, 1224 = (68/100) × (10x - 120)

⇒ 10x - 120 = 1800

⇒ x = 192

The number of 'Inkjet' printers sold in January = 5 × 192 = 960

The number of 'Laser' printers sold in January = 960 - 120 = 840

The total number of printers sold in January = 960 + 840 = 1800

The number of 'Inkjet' printers sold in February = 3 × 192 = 576

The number of 'Laser' printers sold in February = 1224 - 576 = 648

The ratio of the total number of printers (inkjet + laser) sold in January to that in March is 75 : 46 respectively.

Therefore, the total number of printers sold in March = (46/75) × 1800 = 1104

The number of 'laser' printers sold in March is 30% more than the number of 'Inkjet' printers sold in the same month.

So, the number of 'Inkjet' printers sold in March = (10/23) × 1104 = 480

The number of 'Laser' printers sold in March = 1104 - 480 = 624

Putting all the values in a table we get

Month The number of 'Inkjet' printers sold The number of 'Laser' printers sold  The total number of printers sold
January 960 840 1800
February 576 648 1224
March 480 624 1104

The average number of printers sold by the shopkeepers from January to March = 4128/3 = 1376

The total number of printers sold in April month = 1376 + 124 = 1500

Hence, the correct answer is 1500.

Train A is half the length of train B and moves at one-third of train B's speed. If train A takes 48 seconds to pass a man, how much time will it take for train B to pass train A if they are both moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation:
Let the length of train B be 2X meters and the speed of train B be 3Y meters/sec.

Given that the length of train A is half that of train B and the speed of train A is one-third of that of train B.

⇒ The length of train A = 2X/2 = X meters.

⇒ The speed of train A = 3Y/3 = Y meters.

Formula:

Time = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

Relative speed = difference of their speeds (if they go in the same direction)

Concept:

When train A crosses a man, the relative speed of train A with respect to the man is the speed of train A minus speed of man (=0 as he is at rest) which is the same as the speed of train A.

Calculation:

Time taken by train A to cross the man is given as 48 seconds.

Time = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

Time taken to cross the man = Length of train A / Speed of train A

 ⇒ 48 = Length of train A / Y

Length of train A = 48Y

Also, we know that the length of train A is X meters, so we can write:

⇒ 48Y = X

⇒ Y = X/48

Now, we can calculate the time taken by train B to cross train A using the formula:

Time taken by train B = Total distance to be covered / Relative speed

Total distance to be covered = Length of train A + Length of train B

Total distance to be covered = X + 2X = 3X

Relative speed of train B with respect to train A = Speed of train B - Speed of train A

Relative speed of train B with respect to train A = 3Y - Y = 2Y

Time taken by train B = 3X / 2Y

Substituting Y = X/48,

⇒ Time taken by train B = 3X / 2(X/48) = 72

Time taken by train B = 72 seconds = 60 + 12 = 1 minute 12 secs

Therefore, train B will take 1 minute 12 seconds to cross train A if they go in the same direction. Hence, the answer is 1 minute 12 seconds.

questions.text: A certain sum is deposited at a rate of 40% compounded annually. The difference between interest earned in the 1st year and 2nd year is Rs 384. Find the sum.
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

In compound interest, the difference between the interest of consecutive years is the interest on the interest of the previous year.

Difference = 1st year interest × Rate%

384 = (Principal × 40%) × 40%

384 = P × 0.4 × 0.4 ⇒ 384 = P × 0.16

P = 384 ÷ 0.16 = 2400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.

Alternate Method

Given: Rate (R) = 40%, Difference (D) = Rs. 384

Formula: CI for 1st year = P × (R/100); CI for 2nd year = [P + CI1] × (R/100)

⇒ Let Principal be P.

⇒ Interest for 1st year (I1) = P × 40/100 = 0.4P

⇒ Interest for 2nd year (I2) = (P + 0.4P) × 40/100 = 1.4P × 0.4 = 0.56P

⇒ Difference = I2 − I1 = 0.56P − 0.4P = 0.16P

⇒ 0.16P = 384

⇒ P = 384 ÷ 0.16 = 2400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage for CI

For a rate r%, the effective 2-year CI rate is r + r + (r×r)/100. For 40%, it is 40 + 40 + 16 = 96%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is P(R/100)2. In this question, notice that the 1st year CI is equal to the 1st year SI.

Interest on Interest

Compound interest grows because the interest earned in previous periods itself earns interest at the given rate in subsequent periods.

questions.text: In how many ways a cricket team of 11 cricketers containing 1 wicket keeper, 4 bowlers, 4 batsmen and 2 all rounders can be formed from a group of 24 cricketers containing 2 wicket keepers, 7 bowlers, 6 all rounders and 9 batsmen?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

Total ways = 2C1 × 7C4 × 9C4 × 6C2

Total ways = 2 × 35 × 126 × 15

Total ways = 70 × 1890 = 132300

∴ The correct answer is 132300.

Alternate Method

Given:

Wicket Keepers (WK): 2 available, 1 to be selected.

Bowlers (BW): 7 available, 4 to be selected.

Batsmen (BT): 9 available, 4 to be selected.

All Rounders (AR): 6 available, 2 to be selected.

Formula used: nCr = n! / [r! × (n − r)!]

⇒ Ways to select WK = 2C1 = 2! / (1! × 1!) = 2

⇒ Ways to select BW = 7C4 = 7C3 = (7 × 6 × 5) / (3 × 2 × 1) = 35

⇒ Ways to select BT = 9C4 = (9 × 8 × 7 × 6) / (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 126

⇒ Ways to select AR = 6C2 = (6 × 5) / (2 × 1) = 15

⇒ Total ways = 2 × 35 × 126 × 15

⇒ Total ways = 70 × 1890 = 132300

∴ The correct answer is 132300.

Additional Information

Combination Property

The formula nCr = nCn-r is highly useful for simplifying calculations when r is more than half of n.

Fundamental Principle of Counting

If one task can be done in 'm' ways and another in 'n' ways, then both can be done in m × n ways when the tasks are independent.

Preprocessing is the first step. The preprocessor obeys commands that begin with # (known as directives) by:

  • removing comments
  • expanding macros
  • expanding included files

Compiling:

Compiling is the second step. It takes the output of the preprocessor and generates assembly language, an intermediate human-readable language, specific to the target processor.

Assembly:

Assembly is the third step of compilation. The assembler will convert the assembly code into pure binary code or machine code (zeros and ones). This code is also known as object code.

Linking:

Linking is the final step of compilation. The linker merges all the object code from multiple modules into a single one. If we are using a function from libraries, the linker will link our code with that library function code.

questions.text: A relation in which every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the primary key and which has no transitive dependencies is in -
questions.explanation:
1NF:

  • There are only Single Valued Attributes.
  • There is a unique name for every Attribute/Column.

2NF:

  • A relation that is in First Normal Form 
  • Every non-primary-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the primary key 

3NF

  • The third normal form is based on the concept of transitive dependency. A functional dependency X->Y in a relation schema R is a transitive dependency if there exists a set of attributed Z in R that is neither a candidate key nor a subset of any key of R.
  • A relation is in 3NF if it satisfies 2NF and no prime attribute of R is transitively dependent on the primary key.
  • If X - > A is a functional dependency, then A should be a prime attribute or X should be a candidate key.
  • Lossless join and dependency preservation is always possible in 3NF. 3NF decomposition is always lossless join and dependency preserving.

BCNF:

  • It stands for Boyce Codd normal form.
  • A relation R is in BCNF if whenever a non-trivial functional dependency X -> A holds in R, then X is a superkey of R. Any relation with two attributes is always in BCNF. Because when a relation contains only two attributes then one attribute determines another and the left side of the functional dependency will always be a candidate key in that case.
  • BCNF is not always dependency preserving.

Therefore the answer is Option 1.

questions.text: Consider an operating system containing 4 processes and each process requires 3 instances of resource M. What is the minimum number of instances of resource M is needed such that no deadlock will ever occur?
questions.explanation:
Concept:

Deadlock is a situation where a group of processes is permanently blocked as a result of each process having acquired a subset of resources needed for its completion and waiting for the release of remaining resources held by others in the same group.

Explanation:

number of processes = n = 4 process

Each process requires 3 instances of resource X.

Initially, if there is a need for r resources by each process, allocate r -1 resources to each process. Here 3 processes, so each process initially gets 2 resources.  Now total resources allocated are 2 + 2 + 2 + 2= 8

But in this situation, the deadlock will occur. So, increase the resource allocated by 1 so that one of them could complement and release its resource.

Therefore the total number of instances need is 9  so that the deadlock will not occur.

Tips and Tricks :

(∑n1 Pi) - n + 1 = (3 + 3 + 3 + 3) - 4 + 1 = 9

So, the minimum value of M is 9 by which deadlock will not occur.

questions.text: Which of the following media access methods works on first come first served basis?
questions.explanation:
Media access methods:
How a computer terminal on a network gains and controls access to the network's physical medium such as a cable.
 
Some of the common media access methods:
1. CSMA/CD:

  • Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD)
  • Specifies how bus topologies such as Ethernet handle transmission collisions.
  • It usually operates in two modes of Carrier Sense, Multiple Access and Collision Detection.
  • It is in contention, which means any computer in the network can transmit data at any time (first come-first served).


2. CSMA/CA:

  • Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (CSMA/CA)
  • Instead of detecting and reacting to collisions, it tries to avoid them by having each computer signal its intention to transmit before actually transmitting.
  • In effect, the transmitting computer gives a “Request” prior to transmitting.


3. Token Passing:

  • Collisions are eliminated under token passing because only a computer that possesses a free token (a small data frame) is allowed to transmit.
  • The token passing method also allows different priorities to be assigned to different stations on the ring.

The index structure typically provides secondary access path i.e. alternate way of accessing the records without affecting the physical placement of records on disk.

If the ordering field is non-key then it is known as the clustering index. Non-key and ordered means that numerous records in the file can have the same value for the ordering field. The clustering index is also known as the non-dense index.

Clustering index is an ordered file with two fields:

  • First field is of same type as clustering of data file
  • Second field is a block pointer.

A secondary index is defined on an unordered data file. It can be either a candidate key or some non-key field.

questions.text: In OSI model accounting, addressing and routing functions of the system are provided by:
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is OSI Model

Key Points

  • OSI stands for Open System Interconnection is a reference model that describes how information from a software application in one computer moves through a physical medium to the software application in another computer.
  • OSI consists of seven layers, and each layer performs a particular network function.
  • OSI model was developed by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in 1984, and it is now considered as an architectural model for inter-computer communications.

Additional Information

There are seven OSI layers. Each layer has different functions. A list of seven layers are given below:

1) Physical Layer: 

  • The main functionality of the physical layer is to transmit the individual bits from one node to another node.
  • It is the lowest layer of the OSI model.

2) Data-Link Layer: 

  • This layer is responsible for the error-free transfer of data frames.
  • It defines the format of the data on the network.
  • It provides reliable and efficient communication between two or more devices.

3) Network Layer: 

  • It is a layer 3 that manages device addressing, tracks the location of devices on the network.
  • It determines the best path to move data from source to destination based on the network conditions, the priority of service, and other factors.

4) Transport Layer: 

  • The Transport layer is a Layer 4 ensures that messages are transmitted in the order in which they are sent and there is no duplication of data.
  • The main responsibility of the transport layer is to transfer the data completely.

5) Session Layer:

  • The Session layer is used to establish, maintain, and synchronizes the interaction between communicating devices.

​6) Presentation Layer:

  • It acts as a data translator for a network.
  • This layer is a part of the operating system that converts the data from one presentation format to another format.

7) Application Layer: 

  • An application layer serves as a window for users and application processes to access network service.
  • This layer provides network services to the end-users.
  • HTTP is an application layer protocol designed within the framework of the Internet protocol suite. Its definition presumes an underlying and reliable transport layer protocol, and Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is commonly used.

​Thus, HTTP is an application layer in the OSI Model of Networking.
